name: SIMT GPU with graphics, stage G2d: video memory, a VGA display controller, gfx.cfg, pix with blending, a raster unit, a texture unit and a depth test

blocks.name: warp_sched
blocks.description: Warp scheduler, round robin. A warp is ready when it is active, has no instruction in flight and is not waiting at a barrier: ready = active & ~inflight & ~waiting (bit w for warp w). When enable is 1 and some warp is ready, fire = 1 and fwid is the first ready warp in the order ptr+1, ptr+2, ptr+3, ptr+4 (modulo 4), where ptr is a 2-bit register holding the warp chosen last; otherwise fire = 0 and fwid = 0. fire and fwid follow the inputs and ptr at once (combinationally). On each rising edge: when rst or start is 1, ptr becomes 3 (so warp 0 is chosen first); otherwise when fire is 1, ptr becomes fwid; otherwise ptr keeps its value.

blocks.name: warp_table
blocks.description: Per-warp state for 4 warps: a 32-bit pc, a 4-bit thread mask and an in-flight bit each. A warp is active when its mask is not 0. Outputs, combinational from the state and fwid: sel_pc and sel_tmask are warp fwid's pc and mask; active and inflight have one bit per warp (bit w for warp w); busy is 1 when any warp is active or in flight. On each rising edge, the first of these that applies: (1) rst is 1: every pc, mask and in-flight bit becomes 0. (2) start is 1: warp 0 gets pc = start_pc, mask 0001; warps 1 to 3 get pc 0 and mask 0000; every in-flight bit becomes 0. (3) otherwise three independent events apply, all computed from the values before this edge (a later event overrides an earlier one only on the field it names): - commit (when commit is 1): warp cwid gets pc = c_pc, mask = c_tmask and in-flight = 0. - fire (when fire is 1): warp fwid's in-flight bit becomes 1. It does not depend on spawn_mask and does not stop a spawn. - spawn: each warp w with spawn_mask bit w = 1 whose mask was 0000 and whose in-flight bit was 0 before this edge gets pc = spawn_pc and mask = 0001 (its in-flight bit is not touched by spawn). A spawn's pc and mask override a commit's on the same warp; this cannot happen in operation, but the block defines it.

blocks.name: pipe_ctrl
blocks.description:
Pipeline control, combinational. The X stage is busy while it holds a division whose result is not ready, a memory access
    the load-store unit has not finished, or while the graphics units ask for another cycle (g_busy, the texture unit's
    one-cycle read): x_busy = (dx_valid & ((unit is DIV & div_ready is 0) | (unit is LSU & lsu_ready is 0))) | g_busy, with unit
    read through its encoding table. stall = x_busy (the S, D and X stages hold their instructions). advance = dx_valid &
    !x_busy: the instruction in X completes at the next rising edge. sched_en = running & !x_busy. fetch_idx = bits 10:2 of sf_pc
    when x_busy is 1, otherwise bits 10:2 of sel_pc: the instruction-memory word to read, so that a held D stage keeps seeing its
    own instruction.

blocks.name: sf_reg
blocks.description: S/D pipeline register, between the warp scheduler and the decoder. Every output <f>_out shows the value its input <f>_in had at the last rising clock edge at which the register loaded; no output depends combinationally on any input. On each rising edge: when rst is 1 or clear is 1 every field becomes 0 (so valid_out becomes 0: a bubble); otherwise when hold is 1 every field keeps its value; otherwise every field takes its input. The fields: valid (1 bits), wid (2 bits), pc (32 bits), tmask (4 bits).

blocks.name: decode
blocks.description: Instruction decoder, combinational, for RV32IM with CSR reads and the GPU's SIMT (custom-0, opcode 0x0B) and tensor (custom-1, opcode 0x2B) instructions. Fields copied from inst every time: rs1 = bits 19:15, rs2 = bits 24:20, rd = bits 11:7, csr_addr = bits 31:20, br_op = mem_size = simt_op = funct3 (bits 14:12), md_op = funct3 bits 1:0, tensor_op = funct3 bits 1:0, gfx_op = funct3 (bits 14:12), simt_mode = instruction bits 26:25 (the two lowest bits of funct7). Every other output has a default unless the instruction's class below sets it: unit NONE, alu_op ADD, a_sel 0, b_sel 0, immsel NO_IMMEDIATE, wb_src ALU, regwrite 0, ctrl NONE, mem_store 0, illegal 0, gfx 0. The classes (op = bits 6:0, f3 = funct3, f7 = funct7): LUI (0x37): unit ALU, alu_op PASS_B, b_sel 1, immsel IMM_U, regwrite 1. AUIPC (0x17): unit ALU, alu_op ADD, a_sel 1, b_sel 1, immsel IMM_U, regwrite 1. JAL (0x6F): unit ALU, a_sel 1, b_sel 1, immsel IMM_J, wb_src LINK, regwrite 1, ctrl JAL. JALR (0x67 with f3 0): unit ALU, b_sel 1, immsel IMM_I, wb_src LINK, regwrite 1, ctrl JALR. Branch (0x63, f3 not 2 or 3): unit ALU, immsel IMM_B, ctrl BRANCH. Load (0x03, f3 0, 1, 2, 4 or 5): unit LSU, b_sel 1, immsel IMM_I, wb_src LOAD, regwrite 1. Store (0x23, f3 0, 1 or 2): unit LSU, b_sel 1, immsel IMM_S, mem_store 1. OP-IMM (0x13): b_sel 1, immsel IMM_I, regwrite 1, unit ALU, alu_op by f3: 0 ADD, 2 SLT, 3 SLTU, 4 XOR, 6 OR, 7 AND, 1 SLL (only with f7 0), 5 SRL (f7 0) or SRA (f7 0x20); any other f3/f7 is illegal. OP (0x33): regwrite 1; f7 0: unit ALU, alu_op by f3: 0 ADD, 1 SLL, 2 SLT, 3 SLTU, 4 XOR, 5 SRL, 6 OR, 7 AND; f7 0x20 with f3 0: SUB, with f3 5: SRA (unit ALU); f7 0x20 with any f3 other than 0 and 5 (that is 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7) is illegal, as is any f7 other than 0, 0x20 and 1; f7 1: unit MUL with wb_src MUL when f3 < 4, unit DIV with wb_src DIV otherwise; anything else is illegal. FENCE (0x0F, any f3): the defaults (nothing happens). SYSTEM (0x73): f3 2, 3, 6 or 7 with rs1 = 0 is a CSR read: unit CSR, wb_src CSR, regwrite 1; anything else (a CSR write, ecall, ebreak, mret) is illegal. SIMT (0x0B): legal when f3 <= 4 with f7 = 0, or f3 = 5 with f7 <= 2, or f3 = 6 with f7 <= 3: unit SIMT, wb_src SIMT, regwrite 1 for f3 5 and 6 (vote, shuffle), else 0; otherwise illegal. Tensor (0x2B with f7 0 and f3 <= 3): legal when f3 0 has rd = 0, f3 1 always, f3 2 has rd = 0, f3 3 has rd, rs1 and rs2 all 0: unit TENSOR, wb_src TENSOR, regwrite 1 for f3 1, else 0; otherwise illegal. Graphics (opcode 0x5B = 7'b1011011, custom-2), only with f7 = 0: f3 0 (gfx.cfg) or 5 (pix) is legal when rd = 0, with gfx = 1 and every other output its default (so unit is NONE and regwrite 0); f3 1 (rast), 3 (rast.edge), 4 (tex) or 6 (ztest) is legal with any rd, rs1 and rs2, with gfx = 1, regwrite = 1 and every other output its default (unit NONE, wb_src ALU); f3 2 or 7, or f7 not 0, is illegal. Any other instruction is illegal. An illegal instruction has every default except illegal = 1.

blocks.name: vmul
blocks.description: Four-lane multiplier, combinational. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). For each lane, with x = lane i of a and z = lane i of b: md_op 0 MUL, the low 32 bits of x * z; 1 MULH, the high 32 bits of the 64-bit product with both signed; 2 MULHSU, x signed and z unsigned; 3 MULHU, both unsigned.

blocks.name: vdiv
blocks.description: Four-lane iterative divider. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). start = valid & (unit is DIV). It has three states, IDLE, BUSY and DONE, and a 5-bit count. ready is 1 exactly in DONE; y is the four results in DONE and 0 otherwise. On each rising edge: when rst or clear is 1, IDLE. In IDLE with start: take a, b and md_op, count = 0, go to BUSY. In BUSY: when count is 31 go to DONE, otherwise count + 1 (BUSY lasts exactly 32 cycles, one quotient bit per cycle). In DONE with advance: IDLE. The result for each lane, with x = lane i of a and z = lane i of b (RISC-V M): md_op 0 DIV, signed, rounding toward zero, x / 0 = all ones and -2^31 / -1 = -2^31; 1 DIVU, unsigned, x / 0 = all ones; 2 REM, signed with the sign of x, x rem 0 = x and -2^31 rem -1 = 0; 3 REMU, unsigned, x remu 0 = x.

blocks.name: branch_unit
blocks.description: Branch unit, combinational. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). The warp follows its lowest-numbered active lane l (bit l of tmask). When tmask is 0 there is no active lane and next_pc = pc + 4, diverged = 0, whatever ctrl says. link = pc + 4. next_pc by ctrl's encoding table: NONE pc + 4; BRANCH pc + imm when taken bit l is 1, else pc + 4; JAL pc + imm; JALR (lane l of a + imm) with bit 0 cleared. diverged = 1 when the active lanes do not all agree: for BRANCH, when their taken bits differ; for JALR, when their targets (lane value of a + imm) differ; it is 0 for JAL and NONE and when no lane is active (a branch on lane-dependent data, which the instruction set forbids); it changes nothing else.

semantics.description: How the next pc is chosen.

encoding.01: BRANCH: pc + imm when the branch is taken, else pc + 4

blocks.name: vote_shfl
blocks.description: Vote and shuffle unit, combinational. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). When simt_op is VOTE: ballot = the 4-bit mask of lanes active in tmask whose 32-bit lane of a is not 0; each of the four 32-bit lanes of y (bits 32l+31..32l) gets the same 32-bit value, the following zero-extended to 32 bits, by simt_mode: 0 any (1 when ballot is not 0, else 0), 1 all (1 when ballot equals tmask), 2 ballot itself, 3 zero. When simt_op is SHFL: lane l of y = lane s of a, whatever the mask, where k = lane l of b (unsigned) and by simt_mode: 0 s = k mod 4; 1 s = (l xor k) mod 4; 2 s = l - k, or l when k > l; 3 s = l + k, or l when l + k >= 4. Here k is the whole 32-bit unsigned value: for modes 2 and 3 any k of 4 or more (any of bits 31:2 set) gives s = l. Any other simt_op: y = 0.

blocks.name: simt_ctrl
blocks.description: SIMT control, combinational: the warp's next pc and thread mask at commit, and the requests to the divergence stack, the warp table and the barriers. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). fa and fb are lane l of a and of b, for the lowest-numbered active lane l, chosen with four select wires: sel0 = tmask[0] OR (tmask == 4'b0000); sel1 = !tmask[0] AND tmask[1]; sel2 = !tmask[0] AND !tmask[1] AND tmask[2]; sel3 = !tmask[0] AND !tmask[1] AND !tmask[2] AND tmask[3]. Note that when tmask is 4'b0000 sel0 is 1 and the others are 0, so fa and fb are lane 0 (not lane 3, not 0): the same lane 0 that is used when lane 0 is active. p4 = pc + 4. When valid is 0 or unit is not SIMT: c_pc = br_next_pc, c_tmask = tmask and every other output is 0. Otherwise c_pc = p4 and c_tmask = tmask unless set below, and by simt_op: TMC: c_tmask = fa bits 3:0; clear = 1 when that is 0 (the warp ends and its stack empties). WSPAWN: spawn_mask bit w (w = 1, 2, 3) = 1 when w < fa (unsigned), bit 0 = 0; spawn_pc = fb. SPLIT: pred = the active lanes whose a lane is not 0, T = tmask & pred, F = tmask & ~pred. When depth + n > 8 (depth is a 4-bit input that never exceeds 8 in operation, but the sum is compared without wrapping), where n is 2 when both T and F are non-empty and 1 otherwise: err = 1 and nothing is pushed. Otherwise push = n with e0 = (mask tmask, pc 0, fall 1). When n is 2 (both T and F non-empty): e1 = (mask F, pc p4, fall 0) and c_tmask = T. When n is 1 (every active lane agrees, so T or F is empty): there is no e1 and c_tmask = tmask, unchanged, even if the predicate is false in every lane (T is then empty, but the mask does not become 0). JOIN: when depth is 0, err = 1; otherwise pop = 1, c_tmask = top_mask, and c_pc = p4 when top_fall is 1, else top_pc. BAR: bar_arrive = 1, bar_id = fa bits 1:0, bar_count = fb when fb < 7, else 7; err = 1 when fa > 3. VOTE, SHFL and the code 111: nothing more. push, pop, clear, spawn_mask and bar_arrive are forced to 0 whenever advance is 0, so they act only at the edge where the instruction completes. Only those five depend on advance. All the other outputs (c_pc, c_tmask, e0_*, e1_*, spawn_pc, bar_id, bar_count, err) are computed as above whatever advance is, including when advance is 0: for example a BAR with fa > 3 has err = 1 and bar_count set, and a WSPAWN has spawn_pc = fb, even when advance is 0. Every unset field of e0 and e1 is 0.

blocks.name: ipdom
blocks.description: Divergence stacks: one stack of up to 8 entries for each of the 4 warps; an entry is a 4-bit mask, a 32-bit pc and a fall bit. Outputs, combinational from the state and wid: depth (0 to 8) of warp wid's stack, and its top entry (the one pushed last) as top_mask, top_pc and top_fall, all 0 when the stack is empty. On each rising edge: when rst or clear_all is 1, every stack becomes empty. Otherwise, when en is 1, on warp wid's stack, the first of these that applies: clear empties it; pop removes the top entry (nothing when empty); push 1 adds e0; push 2 adds e0 and then e1 (so e1 is on top). A push that would take the stack past 8 entries changes nothing.

blocks.name: barrier_unit
blocks.description: Barriers: four barriers, each with a 4-bit arrived mask (bit w: warp w has arrived), and a 4-bit waiting register (bit w: warp w waits), which is the output. On each rising edge: when rst or clear_all is 1, every arrived mask and waiting bit becomes 0. Otherwise when en is 1: let m = arrived[bar_id] | (1 << wid). When the number of 1 bits in m is at least bar_count, the barrier releases: arrived[bar_id] becomes 0 and every warp in m stops waiting (waiting &= ~m). Otherwise arrived[bar_id] becomes m and warp wid waits (its waiting bit becomes 1).

blocks.name: tensor_unit
blocks.description: Tensor unit. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). For each of the 4 warps, a 4 x 4 accumulator ACC of 32-bit values (lane i owns row i). is_t = valid & (unit is TENSOR). Outputs, combinational: err = is_t & (tmask is not 1111); lane i of ld_y = ACC[wid][i][c] where c = lane i of a, bits 1:0 (whatever the operation). On each rising edge: when rst or clear_all is 1, every accumulator becomes 0. Otherwise when advance & is_t & !err, by tensor_op: MMA_I8: ACC[wid][i][j] += the sum over k = 0..3 of A[i][k] * B[k][j] (32-bit wrapping), where A[i][k] is byte k (bits 8k+7..8k) of lane i of a and B[k][j] is byte k of lane j of b, both signed 8-bit; this is one 4 x 4 x 4 multiply-accumulate per instruction (64 products). MMA_LD: nothing changes. MMA_ST: ACC[wid][i][c] = lane i of a for every lane i, where c = lane i of b, bits 1:0. MMA_ZERO: every entry of ACC[wid] becomes 0. Exact indexing, to avoid transposing: A[i][k] = byte k of lane i of a = a[32*i + 8*k + 7 : 32*i + 8*k] (row i of A comes from lane i of a); B[k][j] = byte k of lane j of b = b[32*j + 8*k + 7 : 32*j + 8*k] (column j of B comes from lane j of b: the lane picks the column j and the byte picks k, never the other way round). Each product A[i][k] * B[k][j] is a SIGNED 8-bit by signed 8-bit product (a signed 16-bit value), sign-extended to 32 bits before it is added; the four products and the old ACC[wid][i][j] are added as 32-bit two's-complement values (wrapping). ACC entry (wid, i, j) is element 16*wid + 4*i + j of the flat array. In MMA_LD / ld_y and MMA_ST the column c of lane i is a[32*i + 1 : 32*i] and b[32*i + 1 : 32*i] respectively. Worked example (after MMA_ZERO, one MMA_I8, wid 0, tmask 1111): a = {lane3: 0, lane2: 32'h000000FF, lane1: 32'h00000002, lane0: 32'h0302FF01} (lane 0 holds A[0][0..3] = 1, -1, 2, 3); b = {lane3: 0, lane2: 0, lane1: 32'h01010101, lane0: 32'h07FA0504} (lane 0 holds B[0..3][0] = 4, 5, -6, 7; lane 1 holds B[0..3][1] = 1, 1, 1, 1). Then ACC[0][0][0] = 1*4 + (-1)*5 + 2*(-6) + 3*7 = 8; ACC[0][0][1] = 1 - 1 + 2 + 3 = 5; ACC[0][1][0] = 2*4 = 8; ACC[0][1][1] = 2*1 = 2; ACC[0][2][0] = -1*4 = -4 = 32'hFFFFFFFC; ACC[0][2][1] = -1 = 32'hFFFFFFFF; every other entry is 0. Implementation note: hold the 64 accumulator entries as a flat 1-D array or as separate registers (no multi-dimensional arrays), so that every simulator reads them correctly.

blocks.name: lsu
blocks.description: Load-store unit for global memory (4 banks of 512 words) and shared memory (4 banks of 256 words); bank k holds the words whose address bits 3:2 are k. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). Packed bank ports: bank k uses bit k of g_en, g_we, s_en and s_we; bits 9k+8..9k of g_addr; bits 8k+7..8k of s_addr; bits 32k+31..32k of g_wdata, s_wdata, g_rdata and s_rdata; bits 4k+3..4k of g_be and s_be. A bank's rdata shows the word it was addressed with in the previous cycle. act = valid & (unit is LSU). Lane i's address A = lane i of a + imm (32 bits); n bytes = 1 for mem_size 0 and 4, 2 for 1 and 5, 4 otherwise. A lane is in global memory when 0x1000_0000 <= A < 0x1000_2000 (word index (A - 0x1000_0000) >> 4) and in shared memory when 0x2000_0000 <= A < 0x2000_1000 (word index (A - 0x2000_0000) >> 4); its bank is A bits 3:2 and its byte offset A bits 1:0. err = act & !started & (some lane active in tmask has A mod n != 0 or is in neither memory). Registers: started (1 bit), pend (4: lanes still to access), got (4: lanes whose loaded word arrives this cycle), cap (128). P = tmask when started is 0, else pend. Requests, only when act & !err: for each memory and each bank, the lowest-numbered lane in P mapped to it is chosen and drives that bank: en 1, we = mem_store, addr = its word index, wdata = (lane i of b) << (8 * offset) truncated to 32 bits, be = ((1 << n) - 1) << offset (4 bits). Every other bank field is 0. Loaded data: cur = cap with each lane in got replaced by its n bytes at its offset in its bank's rdata, sign-extended for mem_size 0 and 1 and zero-extended otherwise; y = cur. ready = act & (err | (mem_store & every lane of P is chosen in this cycle) | (!mem_store & started & P == 0)). On each rising edge: when rst is 1, started = 0, pend = 0, got = 0 and cap = 0; when clear or advance is 1 (and rst is 0) started = 0, pend = 0, got = 0 and cap keeps its value. Otherwise when act & !err: started = 1, pend = P without the chosen lanes, got = the chosen lanes for a load (0 for a store), cap = cur. So an access with one lane per bank takes one cycle to store and two to load; each extra lane in one bank costs a cycle, and lanes in the same bank are served in lane order (for a store to one address, the highest lane's value stays).

semantics.description: Which execution unit an instruction uses.

encoding.000: ALU: the arithmetic unit (also used by jumps and branches)
encoding.111: NONE: no unit (fence, or an illegal instruction)

blocks.name: bank_mux
blocks.description: Memory port switch, combinational. While running is 1 the load-store unit owns the eight banks: global bank k gets we = g_en bit k & g_we bit k, and addr, wdata and be from field k of the packed g_addr, g_wdata and g_be (bank k: bits 9k+8..9k of g_addr, 32k+31..32k of g_wdata, 4k+3..4k of g_be); shared bank k likewise from the s_ ports (bits 8k+7..8k of s_addr). The instruction memory's write port is off: imem_we is 0 (and imem_waddr and imem_wdata are don't-care whenever imem_we is 0). The host's ranges, as bit slices of host_addr (use exactly these): instruction memory when host_addr bits 31:11 are all 0 (21 bits, 0); global memory when bits 31:13 equal 19'h08000 (19 bits); shared memory when bits 31:12 equal 20'h20000 (20 bits). While running is 0 the host owns them, one 32-bit word at a time: when host_addr is in 0x0000_0000..0x0000_07FF, imem_we = host_en & host_we, imem_waddr = host_addr bits 10:2, imem_wdata = host_wdata. When it is in 0x1000_0000..0x1000_1FFF, global bank k = host_addr bits 3:2 gets addr = (host_addr - 0x1000_0000) >> 4, we = host_en & host_we, wdata = host_wdata and be = 1111. When it is in 0x2000_0000..0x2000_0FFF, shared bank k = host_addr bits 3:2 likewise with addr = (host_addr - 0x2000_0000) >> 4. In host mode every bank the host is not addressing has we = 0, and its addr, wdata and be are don't-care. In load-store mode every port is as the packed ports give it. Always: g_rdata packs the four global banks' rdata (bank k in bits 32k+31..32k), and s_rdata the four shared banks'.

blocks.name: gbank0
blocks.description: Global memory bank 0 (the words whose address bits 3:2 are 0): 512 words of 32 bits, with a byte enable per byte.

blocks.name: gbank1
blocks.description: Global memory bank 1 (the words whose address bits 3:2 are 1): 512 words of 32 bits, with a byte enable per byte.

blocks.name: gbank2
blocks.description: Global memory bank 2 (the words whose address bits 3:2 are 2): 512 words of 32 bits, with a byte enable per byte.

blocks.name: gbank3
blocks.description: Global memory bank 3 (the words whose address bits 3:2 are 3): 512 words of 32 bits, with a byte enable per byte.

blocks.name: sbank0
blocks.description: Shared memory bank 0 (the words whose address bits 3:2 are 0): 256 words of 32 bits, with a byte enable per byte.

blocks.name: sbank1
blocks.description: Shared memory bank 1 (the words whose address bits 3:2 are 1): 256 words of 32 bits, with a byte enable per byte.

blocks.name: sbank2
blocks.description: Shared memory bank 2 (the words whose address bits 3:2 are 2): 256 words of 32 bits, with a byte enable per byte.

blocks.name: sbank3
blocks.description: Shared memory bank 3 (the words whose address bits 3:2 are 3): 256 words of 32 bits, with a byte enable per byte.

blocks.name: wb_mux
blocks.description: Write-back selector, combinational. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). Let w = advance & regwrite & (rd != 0) and r = the source wb_src's encoding table selects: alu_y, mul_y, div_y, load_y, simt_y, tensor_y, csr_y, or link in every lane. For each lane k: we_k = w & tmask bit k (only active lanes write) and wdata_k = lane k of r. waddr = wid * 32 + rd.

semantics.description: Which result is written back to the register file.

encoding.011: LOAD: the load-store unit's loaded value
encoding.101: TENSOR: the tensor unit's accumulator column

blocks.name: host_if
blocks.description: Host interface. The host bus: host_en, host_we, host_addr, host_wdata in; host_rdata and host_rvalid out; a read's data comes in the cycle after the request, with host_rvalid = 1. Registers: running, done, error (1 bit each), start_pc, karg, err_pc (32 bits), err_info (10 bits), rvalid (1) and raddr (32). Control addresses: 0x3000_0000 CTRL (write bit 0 = 1 to start), 0x3000_0004 START_PC, 0x3000_0008 KARG, 0x3000_000C STATUS (bit 0 running, bit 1 done, bit 2 error), 0x3000_0010 ERR_PC, 0x3000_0014 ERR_INFO. ERR_INFO is 10 bits wide, laid out as: bits 3:0 the cause (a number 0 to 5), bits 7:4 always 0, bits 9:8 the warp x_wid (2 bits). As a concatenation: err_info <= {x_wid, 4'b0000, cause[3:0]}. Example: cause 3 in warp 2 gives err_info = 10'b10_0000_0011 (0x203); cause 1 in warp 0 gives 10'b00_0000_0001 (0x001). Outputs: running, done, error, start_pc and karg show their registers; host_rvalid shows rvalid; start (combinational) = host_en & host_we & (host_addr == 0x3000_0000) & host_wdata bit 0 & !running. The cause of an error is the first of err_illegal (1), err_mem (2), err_simt (3), err_tensor (4), err_csr (5) that is 1, or 0 when none is. On each rising edge: when rst is 1 every register becomes 0. Otherwise: a host write (host_en & host_we) while running is 0 to START_PC or KARG stores host_wdata there. Then the first that applies: start: running 1, done 0, error 0; running & advance & a cause: running 0, error 1, err_pc = x_pc, err_info = {x_wid, 4'b0000, cause[3:0]} (the cause in the low 4 bits, the warp in bits 9:8); running & !busy: running 0, done 1. And always rvalid = host_en & !host_we and raddr = host_addr. host_rdata, combinational from raddr: when raddr is in 0x1000_0000..0x1000_1FFF, word (raddr bits 3:2) of g_rdata (bits 32k+31..32k for word k); in 0x2000_0000..0x2000_0FFF the same of s_rdata; at a control address its register's present value (STATUS as described, CTRL reads 0); anywhere else 0.

blocks.name: gfx_host
blocks.description: Host-bus side of the graphics hardware. The host bus: host_en, host_we, host_addr (32), host_wdata (32) in; a read's data is shown on host_rdata in the cycle after the request. core_rdata is the GPU core's own read data for that same request (it already follows the one-cycle rule), shown unchanged for every address this block does not own. Registers, all 0 after reset: raddr (32 bits, the address of the last host request) and disp_en (1 bit). The video memory window: host_addr is in it when host_addr bits 31:18 equal 14'h1000 (0x4000_0000 .. 0x4003_FFFF), host_addr bits 17:0 are less than 18'h25800, and host_addr bits 1:0 are 00. Such a word holds two pixels: its low half (bits 15:0) is pixel p = host_addr bits 17:1 (an even number) and its high half (bits 31:16) is pixel p + 1. Pixel p is in bank p mod 4 at index p / 4, so the word goes to banks 0 (low half) and 1 (high half) when host_addr bit 2 is 0, and to banks 2 (low half) and 3 (high half) when host_addr bit 2 is 1, at index host_addr bits 17:3 in both. Combinational outputs: v_waddr = host_addr bits 17:3 (15 bits); vw_raddr = host_addr bits 17:3 (15 bits); v_wdata_lo = host_wdata bits 15:0; v_wdata_hi = host_wdata bits 31:16; with wr = host_en & host_we & (host_addr is in the video memory window): v_we0 = wr & !host_addr bit 2; v_we1 = wr & !host_addr bit 2; v_we2 = wr & host_addr bit 2; v_we3 = wr & host_addr bit 2. disp_en shows its register. host_rdata, combinational from the register raddr: when raddr is in the video memory window (the same three tests applied to raddr), {vw_rdata1, vw_rdata0} when raddr bit 2 is 0, {vw_rdata3, vw_rdata2} when raddr bit 2 is 1 (the first named is bits 31:16); when raddr is 32'h3000_0020 (DISP_CTRL), {31'b0, disp_en}; when raddr is 32'h3000_0024 (DISP_STATUS), {16'b0, frame (8 bits), 7'b0, vblank}; anywhere else core_rdata. On each rising edge: when rst is 1 raddr = 0 and disp_en = 0. Otherwise raddr = host_addr (on every edge, whether or not host_en is 1), and when host_en & host_we & (host_addr == 32'h3000_0020), disp_en = host_wdata bit 0. Example: a write of 32'hF800_001F to 0x4000_0004 sets v_we2 = v_we3 = 1, v_waddr = 0, v_wdata_lo = 16'h001F (pixel 2, in bank 2) and v_wdata_hi = 16'hF800 (pixel 3, in bank 3). A read of 0x4000_0004 in one cycle, with vw_rdata2 = 16'h001F and vw_rdata3 = 16'hF800 in the next, shows host_rdata = 32'hF800_001F in that next cycle.

blocks.name: disp_ctrl
blocks.description: Display controller: VGA 640 x 480 at 60 Hz timing, one pixel per clock, showing a 320 x 240 image with every pixel doubled in both directions. A line is 800 clocks (640 visible, then 16 front porch, 96 sync, 48 back porch); a frame is 525 lines (480 visible, then 10 front porch, 2 sync, 33 back porch). The image is read from four memory banks: image pixel p = y*320 + x is in bank p mod 4 at index p / 4; all four banks get the same address vd_raddr, and bank k's word shows on vd_rdata<k> in the cycle after the address (a synchronous read). Registers, all 0 after reset: hc (10 bits, the column), vc (10 bits, the line), frame (8 bits), d_hc (10), d_vc (10), d_on (1); d_hc, d_vc and d_on are hc, vc and "enabled" delayed by one clock, so they describe the pixel whose data is arriving on vd_rdata now. On each rising edge: when rst is 1 every register becomes 0. Otherwise, when enable is 0: hc = 0, vc = 0, d_on = 0 (frame, d_hc and d_vc keep their values). Otherwise (enable is 1): d_hc = hc, d_vc = vc, d_on = 1, and the counters step: when hc is 799, hc = 0 and (when vc is 524, vc = 0 and frame = frame + 1, wrapping at 256; otherwise vc = vc + 1); otherwise hc = hc + 1. Combinational outputs: vd_raddr (15 bits) = (vc >> 1) * 80 + (hc >> 3) when hc < 640 and vc < 480, else 0 (each read brings the four image pixels (hc >> 1) & ~3 .. +3 of image line vc >> 1, one per bank). vblank = (vc >= 480). frame shows its register. With vis = d_on & (d_hc < 640) & (d_vc < 480): de = vis; rgb (16 bits) = vd_rdata<k> with k = (d_hc >> 1) & 3 when vis, else 0; hsync = 0 when d_on & (656 <= d_hc < 752), else 1; vsync = 0 when d_on & (490 <= d_vc < 492), else 1 (both syncs are active low). Example: after reset with enable held at 1, at the first edge d_on = 1, d_hc = 0, d_vc = 0 and hc becomes 1; in the next cycle de = 1 and rgb = vd_rdata0 (image pixel 0), and vd_raddr = 0 (hc = 1).

blocks.name: gfx_regs
blocks.description: Graphics state registers set by the gfx.cfg instruction. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). Four 9-bit registers, the scissor box: x0 (register number 0), y0 (1), x1 (2), y1 (3); sc_x0, sc_y0, sc_x1, sc_y1 show them at once. On each rising edge: when rst is 1 or clear is 1, x0 = 0, y0 = 0, x1 = 320, y1 = 240. Otherwise, when valid & advance & gfx are 1 and gfx_op is 0 (gfx.cfg) and tmask is not 0: take the lowest-numbered lane l whose tmask bit is 1; the register number is the 32-bit lane l of a and the value is the 32-bit lane l of b; when the number is 0, 1, 2 or 3 that register takes value bits 8:0, and for any other number nothing changes. The unit's other inputs do not matter.

blocks.name: rop_unit
blocks.description: Raster-output unit: the pix instruction, combinational. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). act = valid & advance & gfx & (gfx_op is 5). When act is 0 every output is 0. Otherwise each lane l whose tmask bit l is 1 takes position = the 32-bit lane l of a (x = bits 15:0, y = bits 31:16, both unsigned) and colour = the 32-bit lane l of b (ARGB8888: alpha bits 31:24 are ignored, r = bits 23:16, g = bits 15:8, b = bits 7:0). The lane draws when x < 320, y < 240, sc_x0 <= x, x < sc_x1, sc_y0 <= y and y < sc_y1 (the scissor box, 9-bit values). A drawing lane writes the video-memory bank k = x bits 1:0 at index y * 80 + (x >> 2) (15 bits) the 16-bit value {r bits 7:3, g bits 7:2, b bits 7:3}. If several drawing lanes have the same bank, the highest-numbered of them is the one written. For each bank k from 0 to 3: r_we<k> = 1 when some lane writes bank k, r_waddr<k> is its index and r_wdata<k> its value; when r_we<k> is 0, r_waddr<k> and r_wdata<k> are 0. Read addresses (for blending): r_raddr<k> is the index the winning lane of bank k has, found by the same rules but with pre = valid & gfx & (gfx_op is 5) in place of act, that is without advance (the read happens in the cycle the pipeline is held); r_raddr<k> is 0 when no lane draws on bank k or pre is 0. Blending: when blend is 1, the value written to bank k is not the plain colour but source-over: a = colour bits 31:24, the destination is vw_rdata<k> of the bank k being written (RGB565, the pixel now in the memory), widened to 8 bits per channel by repeating its top bits: with d = vw_rdata<k>, dr = {d[15:11], d[15:13]}, dg = {d[10:5], d[10:9]}, db = {d[4:0], d[4:2]} (that is r5 << 3 | r5 >> 2, g6 << 2 | g6 >> 4, b5 << 3 | b5 >> 2). For each channel, with s the colour's channel: x = s * a + d * (255 - a) (16 bits), and the channel is (x + 128 + ((x + 128) >> 8)) >> 8 (x / 255 rounded). The three channels are then truncated to RGB565 as in replace mode. When blend is 0, vw_rdata<k> is not used.

blocks.name: vram_mux
blocks.description: Video-memory write-port switch, combinational. While running is 1 the raster-output unit owns the four write ports: for bank k (0 to 3) m_we<k> = r_we<k>, m_waddr<k> = r_waddr<k> and m_wdata<k> = r_wdata<k>. While running is 0 the host does: m_we<k> = v_we<k>, m_waddr<k> = v_waddr, and m_wdata<k> = v_wdata_lo for banks 0 and 2 and v_wdata_hi for banks 1 and 3. The write addresses are values this switch passes through, not addresses it decodes (their port role is data).

blocks.name: raster_regs
blocks.description: Raster unit state, set by gfx.cfg and stepped by rast. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). Registers: the box x0, y0, x1, y1 (9 bits each); nine 32-bit edge coefficients ea0, eb0, ec0, ea1, eb1, ec1, ea2, eb2, ec2 (gfx.cfg numbers 16 to 24 in that order); bias (3 bits, number 25); and for each warp w from 0 to 3 a scan: sx_w and sy_w (10 bits each) and done_w (1 bit). Outputs, at once: ea0 to ec2 and bias show their registers; s_x, s_y and s_done show the scan of the warp numbered by the input wid. On each rising edge: when rst is 1 or clear is 1, the box, the coefficients and bias become 0 and every warp's scan becomes sx = 0, sy = 0, done = 1. Otherwise a register changes only when all four hold: valid = 1, advance = 1 (when advance is 0 the pipeline is stalled and nothing changes, whatever the other inputs), gfx = 1 and tmask is not 0. Then, with l the lowest-numbered lane whose tmask bit is 1: - gfx_op 0 (gfx.cfg): the register number n is the 32-bit lane l of a and the value v the 32-bit lane l of b. n = 8: x0 = v bits 8:0 with bits 1:0 cleared, y0 = v bits 24:16, and all four warps' scans restart at once. With nx = v bits 8:2 followed by 2'b00 (the new x0), ny = v bits 24:16 and q = ny bits 1:0, for each warp w = 0, 1, 2, 3 all three of its scan registers are written: sx_w = nx; sy_w = ny - q + w, plus 4 when w < q (the first row at or after ny whose two low bits equal w); done_w = 1 when sy_w > y1 or nx > x1 (x1 and y1 as held before this edge), else 0. Example: ny = 6 (q = 2) gives sy_0 = 8, sy_1 = 9, sy_2 = 6, sy_3 = 7. n = 9: x1 = v bits 8:0 and y1 = v bits 24:16. n = 16 to 24: that coefficient = v. n = 25: bias = v bits 2:0. Any other n: nothing changes. n is compared as a whole 32-bit number: a value such as 0x0000_0114 or 0x8000_0010 is not 20 or 16 and changes nothing. - gfx_op 1 (rast): only warp w = wid's scan changes, and only when done_w is 0: when sx_w + 4 > x1, then sx_w = x0, sy_w = sy_w + 4, and done_w = 1 when that new sy_w > y1; otherwise sx_w = sx_w + 4. - any other gfx_op: nothing changes.

blocks.name: raster_eval
blocks.description: Raster unit evaluator, combinational: the results of rast and rast.edge. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). Edge function i (0, 1 or 2) at pixel (x, y): E_i = ea_i * x + eb_i * y + ec_i, computed in 32 bits (wrapping), with x and y unsigned. The output y has one 32-bit value per lane: - when gfx is 1, gfx_op is 1 (rast) and s_done is 1: every lane is 0xFFFFFFFF (the warp's scan is finished; this case is checked first and wins over the next one). - when gfx is 1, gfx_op is 1 (rast) and s_done is 0: lane l looks at pixel x = s_x + l, row s_y; the pixel is covered when, for each of the three edges, E_i + bias bit i, read as a signed 32-bit number, is greater than 0. Lane l is (s_y << 16) | x when covered and (0xFFFF << 16) | x when not (x and s_y as 16-bit fields). - when gfx is 1 and gfx_op is 3 (rast.edge): lane l takes the position p = the 32-bit lane l of a (x = p bits 15:0, y = p bits 31:16) and the edge number n = bits 1:0 of the 32-bit lane l of b; the lane is E_n at (x, y), or 0 when n is 3. - otherwise every lane is 0. Example: ea0 = 0xFFFFFFF0 (-16), eb0 = 0, ec0 = 100, bias = 0: at x = 6 E_0 = 4 (covered as far as edge 0 goes), at x = 7 E_0 = -12 (not covered).

blocks.name: gfx_sel
blocks.description: Graphics write-back select, combinational: y = gfx_y | tex_y | z_y (bitwise or) when gfx is 1, otherwise y = alu_y (all 128 bits). A graphics instruction's result (the raster unit's gfx_y, the texture unit's tex_y or the depth unit's z_y; each is 0 for instructions that are not its own) takes the place of the arithmetic unit's on its way to the write-back selector.

blocks.name: tex_ctrl
blocks.description: Texture unit control. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). A tex instruction reads synchronous memories, so it holds the pipeline for exactly one cycle. Registers: pending (1 bit) and tex_mode (3 bits, the texture mode set by gfx.cfg number 32: bit 0 bilinear, bit 1 clamp u, bit 2 clamp v). Outputs, at once: g_busy = valid & gfx & (gfx_op is 4) & !pending; tex_mode shows its register. On each rising edge: when rst is 1 or clear is 1, pending = 0 and tex_mode = 0. Otherwise: pending = 0 when advance is 1; else pending = 1 when valid, gfx are 1 and gfx_op is 4; else pending keeps its value. And when valid, advance and gfx are 1, gfx_op is 0 (gfx.cfg) and tmask is not 0: with l the lowest-numbered lane whose tmask bit is 1, when the 32-bit lane l of a equals 32 (compared as a whole 32-bit number), tex_mode = bits 2:0 of the 32-bit lane l of b. So a tex in X sees g_busy = 1 in its first cycle (the pipeline holds), pending becomes 1, and in the next cycle g_busy = 0, the instruction completes, and pending returns to 0.

blocks.name: tex_host
blocks.description: Texture memory host window, combinational, write only. The texture is 32 x 32 texels of 16 bits (RGB565); texel t = ty * 32 + tx is at byte 0x5000_0000 + 2t, so a 32-bit host write at host_addr sets texels 2w (low half of host_wdata) and 2w + 1 (high half), w = host_addr bits 10:2. Texel (tx, ty) lives in bank (ty mod 2) * 2 + (tx mod 2) at index (ty >> 1) * 16 + (tx >> 1). Let hit = host_en & host_we & (0x5000_0000 <= host_addr < 0x5000_0800). Then t_we0 = t_we1 = hit & (host_addr bit 6 is 0), t_we2 = t_we3 = hit & (host_addr bit 6 is 1); t_waddr = {host_addr bits 10:7, host_addr bits 5:2} (8 bits); t_wdata_lo = host_wdata bits 15:0 (for banks 0 and 2) and t_wdata_hi = host_wdata bits 31:16 (for banks 1 and 3). t_waddr and the data outputs follow the inputs whether or not there is a write.

blocks.name: tex_addr
blocks.description: Texture unit read addresses, combinational. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). For each lane l: u = the 32-bit lane l of a and v = the 32-bit lane l of b, unsigned 8.8 fixed point in texels, of which only bits 15:0 count: iu = u bits 15:8, iv = v bits 15:8. Wrap of a coordinate c (0 to 256) on an axis: repeat (tex_mode bit 1 is 0 for u, bit 2 is 0 for v) gives c mod 32, clamp gives min(c, 31). x0 = wrap_u(iu), x1 = wrap_u(iu + 1), y0 = wrap_v(iv), y1 = wrap_v(iv + 1). Lane l has its own four texture banks; bank k = py * 2 + px holds the texels (tx, ty) with ty mod 2 = py and tx mod 2 = px, at index (ty >> 1) * 16 + (tx >> 1). For bank k: xk = x0 when x0 mod 2 = px, otherwise x1; yk = y0 when y0 mod 2 = py, otherwise y1; ta<l><k> = (yk >> 1) * 16 + (xk >> 1) (8 bits). The outputs do not depend on tex_mode bit 0 and are driven all the time. Example: u = 31.5 texels (0x1F80) with repeat: x0 = 31, x1 = 0; bank px = 1 reads x 31, bank px = 0 reads x 0.

blocks.name: tex_filter
blocks.description: Texture unit filter, combinational: the result of tex. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). When gfx is 1 and gfx_op is 4, lane l of tex_y is the texture sample at u = the 32-bit lane l of a, v = the 32-bit lane l of b; otherwise tex_y is 0. The texels come from lane l's four banks, read in the cycle before at the addresses of tex_addr (the pipeline holds the instruction for it): t<l><k> is bank k = py * 2 + px of lane l. iu = u bits 15:8, iv = v bits 15:8, fu = u bits 7:0, fv = v bits 7:0; x0 = wrap_u(iu), x1 = wrap_u(iu + 1), y0 = wrap_v(iv), y1 = wrap_v(iv + 1), where wrap is c mod 32 (repeat) or min(c, 31) (clamp) by tex_mode bit 1 for u and bit 2 for v. The texel at (xX, yY) is t<l><k> with k = (yY mod 2) * 2 + (xX mod 2). Each texel is RGB565 (r5 = bits 15:11, g6 = bits 10:5, b5 = bits 4:0), widened to 8 bits per channel: r8 = r5 << 3 | r5 >> 2, g8 = g6 << 2 | g6 >> 4, b8 = b5 << 3 | b5 >> 2. Point filter (tex_mode bit 0 is 0): the texel (x0, y0). Bilinear (bit 0 is 1): each channel is (c00 * (256 - fu) * (256 - fv) + c10 * fu * (256 - fv) + c01 * (256 - fu) * fv + c11 * fu * fv + 32768) >> 16, where cXY is that channel of the texel (xX, yY). The lane is 0xFF << 24 | r << 16 | g << 8 | b.

blocks.name: rop_ctrl
blocks.description: Raster-output control. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). Registers: blend (1 bit, set by gfx.cfg number 4: 1 source-over, 0 replace) and pending (1 bit). With blending on, pix reads the destination pixel in a first cycle and writes in a second, so it holds the pipeline one cycle. Outputs, at once: blend shows its register; g_busy = tex_busy | (valid & gfx & (gfx_op is 5) & blend & !pending) (the texture unit's request or this unit's, for the pipeline control). On each rising edge: when rst is 1 or clear is 1, blend = 0 and pending = 0. Otherwise: pending = 0 when advance is 1; else pending = 1 when valid and gfx are 1, gfx_op is 5 and blend is 1; else pending keeps its value. And when valid, advance and gfx are 1, gfx_op is 0 (gfx.cfg) and tmask is not 0: with l the lowest-numbered lane whose tmask bit is 1, when the 32-bit lane l of a equals 4 (compared as a whole 32-bit number), blend = bit 0 of the 32-bit lane l of b.

blocks.name: vram_rmux
blocks.description: Video-memory read-address switch for the work copy, combinational. While running is 1 the raster-output unit reads (for blending): m_raddr<k> = r_raddr<k> for each bank k from 0 to 3. While running is 0 the host does: every m_raddr<k> = vw_raddr. The addresses are values this switch passes through (their port role is data).

blocks.name: z_ctrl
blocks.description: Depth unit control. ztest reads the depth memory in a first cycle and compares and writes in a second, so it holds the pipeline one cycle. Register: pending (1 bit). Output, at once: g_busy = in_busy | (valid & gfx & (gfx_op is 6) & !pending), where in_busy is the other graphics units' request, passed on to the pipeline control. On each rising edge: when rst is 1 or clear is 1, pending = 0; otherwise pending = 0 when advance is 1, else pending = 1 when valid and gfx are 1 and gfx_op is 6, else pending keeps its value.

blocks.name: z_unit
blocks.description: Depth unit, combinational: the ztest instruction. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). Every output is 0 unless gfx is 1 and gfx_op is 6. Then, for each lane l (0 to 3) whose tmask bit l is 1: x_l = bits 15:0 and y_l = bits 31:16 of the 32-bit lane l of a (unsigned), and the depth z_l = bits 15:0 of the 32-bit lane l of b. Lane l tests when x_l < 320 and y_l < 240; it then belongs to depth bank x_l bits 1:0 (any of the four banks, whatever l is: lanes and banks are different things) at index y_l * 80 + (x_l >> 2) (15 bits). For each bank k from 0 to 3, look at the lanes in the order 3, 2, 1, 0: the first lane that tests and belongs to bank k is bank k's winner; other lanes of bank k do not test, and bank k has no winner when no testing lane belongs to it. Bank k's winner, lane l, passes when z_l < z_rdata<k> (unsigned 16 bits; z_rdata<k> is bank k's stored depth, read in the cycle before at z_raddr<k>). - z_raddr<k>: when valid is 1 and bank k has a winner, the winner's index; otherwise 0. - Writes, when valid and advance are both 1: for each bank k whose winner passes, zw_we<k> = 1, zw_waddr<k> = the winner's index and zw_wdata<k> = the winner's z. For every other bank, and whenever valid or advance is 0, zw_we<k> = 0, and then zw_waddr<k> and zw_wdata<k> may be anything (they are used only with zw_we<k> = 1). - z_y: the 32-bit lane l of z_y is 0xFFFFFFFF (all ones, a lane mask) when lane l is a passing winner, else 0. It does not depend on valid or advance. Example: lane 0 at x = 6 and lane 2 at x = 10 both belong to bank 2; lane 2 is bank 2's winner and lane 0 does not test.

blocks.name: z_host
blocks.description: Depth memory host window, combinational, write only. A 32-bit host write to 0x4004_0000 <= host_addr < 0x4006_5800 sets the depth of pixels 2w (low half of host_wdata) and 2w + 1 (high half), w = (host_addr - 0x4004_0000) >> 2; pixel p is in bank p mod 4 at index p >> 2. Let hit = host_en & host_we & (0x4004_0000 <= host_addr < 0x4006_5800). Then zh_we0 = zh_we1 = hit & (host_addr bit 2 is 0), zh_we2 = zh_we3 = hit & (host_addr bit 2 is 1); zh_waddr = host_addr bits 17:3 (15 bits); zh_wdata_lo = host_wdata bits 15:0 (for banks 0 and 2) and zh_wdata_hi = host_wdata bits 31:16 (for banks 1 and 3). zh_waddr and the data outputs follow the inputs whether or not there is a write.

blocks.name: z_mux
blocks.description: Depth memory write-port switch, combinational. While running is 1 the depth unit owns the four write ports: for bank k (0 to 3) mz_we<k> = zw_we<k>, mz_waddr<k> = zw_waddr<k> and mz_wdata<k> = zw_wdata<k>. While running is 0 the host does: mz_we<k> = zh_we<k>, mz_waddr<k> = zh_waddr, and mz_wdata<k> = zh_wdata_lo for banks 0 and 2 and zh_wdata_hi for banks 1 and 3. The addresses are values this switch passes through (their port role is data).

referenceMaterial.title: The GPU's instruction set (ISA.md)
referenceMaterial.content:
# BARG SIMT GPU, v0: instruction set

Each thread runs **RV32IM** plus `Zicsr` reads; a warp of 4 threads (lanes) issues one instruction for all its active lanes.
The extensions below follow the semantics of Vortex (Tine et al., MICRO 2021) for `wspawn`, `tmc`, `split`, `join`, `bar`, and
of NVIDIA's PTX `vote.sync` and `shfl.sync` for `vote` and `shfl`; the tensor instructions are a 4-lane version of a warp-level
matrix multiply whose accumulator lives in the unit, as Blackwell's tensor memory (`tcgen05.mma`, `.ld`, `.st`) and Virgo's
accumulator memory do (see `docs/gpu-architecture.md`). **The encodings are this design's own** and are not binary
compatible with Vortex. `demos/simt-gpu/model/simt.py` implements exactly this page; where they differ, one of them is wrong.

## Encodings

All are R-type: `funct7[31:25] rs2[24:20] rs1[19:15] funct3[14:12] rd[11:7] opcode[6:0]`.

| Instruction | opcode | funct3 | funct7 | Operands |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tmc rs1` | `custom-0` 0x0B | 0 | 0 | rd = rs2 = 0 |
| `wspawn rs1, rs2` | 0x0B | 1 | 0 | rd = 0 |
| `split rs1` | 0x0B | 2 | 0 | rd = rs2 = 0 |
| `join` | 0x0B | 3 | 0 | rd = rs1 = rs2 = 0 |
| `bar rs1, rs2` | 0x0B | 4 | 0 | rd = 0 |
| `vote.any rd, rs1` / `vote.all` / `vote.ballot` | 0x0B | 5 | 0 / 1 / 2 | rs2 = 0 |
| `shfl.idx rd, rs1, rs2` / `.xor` / `.up` / `.down` | 0x0B | 6 | 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 | |
| `mma.i8 rs1, rs2` | `custom-1` 0x2B | 0 | 0 | rd = 0 |
| `mma.ld rd, rs1` | 0x2B | 1 | 0 | rs2 = 0 |
| `mma.st rs1, rs2` | 0x2B | 2 | 0 | rd = 0 |
| `mma.zero` | 0x2B | 3 | 0 | rd = rs1 = rs2 = 0 |

Any other funct3/funct7 under these opcodes is an illegal instruction.

## Semantics

*Warp-wide operand* below means: the value of that register in the lowest-numbered active lane.

- **`tmc rs1`**: the thread mask becomes the low 4 bits of the warp-wide `rs1`. A mask of 0 ends the warp (it becomes inactive
  and its divergence stack is cleared).
- **`wspawn rs1, rs2`**: warps 1 .. min(`rs1`, 4) - 1 that are inactive become active at PC = warp-wide `rs2` with only lane 0
  active. Their registers other than x0 are **undefined**. Warps already active are left alone.
- **`split rs1`**: each active lane's predicate is `rs1 != 0`. Let T = active lanes with a true predicate, F = the rest. If both
  are non-empty: push (current mask, fall-through), push (F, PC + 4), set the mask to T. Otherwise push (current mask,
  fall-through) only. Execution continues at PC + 4.
- **`join`**: pop (mask, pc). The thread mask becomes mask; continue at pc, or at PC + 4 for a fall-through entry. A `join`
  with an empty stack is an error. Stack depth: 8 entries per warp; a `split` that would exceed it is an error.
- **`bar rs1, rs2`**: barrier number = warp-wide `rs1` (0..3), expected warps = warp-wide `rs2`. The warp waits until that many
  warps have reached barrier `rs1`; then all of them continue. If every active warp waits and none can be released, the
  core stops with an error (deadlock).
- **`vote.any rd, rs1`**: every active lane gets 1 if any active lane has `rs1 != 0`, else 0. **`vote.all`**: 1 if all active
  lanes do. **`vote.ballot`**: the mask of active lanes with `rs1 != 0`. The result is the same in every active lane, so a
  branch on it is uniform.
- **`shfl.* rd, rs1, rs2`**: lane *l* gets `rs1` of a source lane *s* (read from every lane's register file before any write,
  whether or not lane *s* is active): `.idx` s = `rs2` mod 4; `.xor` s = (l xor `rs2`) mod 4; `.up` s = l - `rs2`, or l if that
  is below 0; `.down` s = l + `rs2`, or l if that is 4 or more. `rs2` is each lane's own value.
- **The tensor unit** keeps, for each warp, a 4 x 4 accumulator of 32-bit values (lane *i* owns row *i*). All four lanes must be
  active for every tensor instruction, and the fields marked 0 above must be 0; otherwise it is an error.
  - **`mma.i8 rs1, rs2`**: ACC += A x B, A and B signed 8-bit (32-bit wrapping sums). Lane *i*'s `rs1` holds row *i* of A
    (element *k* in bits 8k+7..8k); lane *j*'s `rs2` holds column *j* of B (element *k* in bits 8k+7..8k).
  - **`mma.ld rd, rs1`**: lane *i* gets ACC[*i*][`rs1` mod 4].
  - **`mma.st rs1, rs2`**: ACC[*i*][`rs2` mod 4] = lane *i*'s `rs1` (an initial C, or a bias).
  - **`mma.zero`**: ACC = 0. The accumulators are 0 after the host's start.
  Every tensor instruction reads at most two registers and writes at most one, like every other instruction.

## CSRs (read-only; any write is an error)

| Address | Name | Value |
|---|---|---|
| 0xCC0 | `tid` | lane number 0..3 |
| 0xCC1 | `wid` | warp number 0..3 |
| 0xCC2 | `cid` | core number |
| 0xCC3 | `tmask` | the warp's thread mask |
| 0xCC4 | `gtid` | (cid x warps + wid) x lanes + tid |
| 0xCC5 | `karg` | the kernel argument pointer the host wrote |
| 0xFC0, 0xFC1, 0xFC2 | `nt`, `nw`, `nc` | lanes per warp, warps per core, cores |
| 0xC00, 0xC80, 0xC02, 0xC82 | `cycle`, `cycleh`, `instret`, `instreth` | counters |

## Other rules

- **Branches and `jalr` must be uniform** across the active lanes; divergence goes through `split`/`join` (or a `vote`). If
  they are not, the hardware follows the lowest-numbered active lane (the model stops, in strict mode, to catch the bug).
- **Threads of one warp must not wait on each other** (no spin locks inside a warp): the pre-Volta SIMT-stack rule.
- **Stores from several lanes to one address** in one instruction: the highest-numbered lane's value is kept.
- **Memory map** (one core): instruction memory 0x0000_0000, 2 KB (fetch only); global memory 0x1000_0000, 8 KB; shared memory
  0x2000_0000, 4 KB in 4 banks interleaved by word. Misaligned accesses and accesses outside data memory are errors.
- **Memory contents are undefined until written.** A kernel must not read data the host or the kernel itself has not written (the model and
  the behavioural RTL start at zero, but SRAM macros do not: `docs/gpu-sram-macros.md`).
- `fence` does nothing (no caches); `ecall`, `ebreak`, `mret` and the privileged CSRs do not exist (illegal).
- **Start and end**: the host loads the memories, writes the start PC and `karg`, and starts warp 0 with lane 0 active. The
  core reports "done" when no warp is active, or "error" with the PC and warp of the faulting instruction.
